details: Russia conducted an extensive drone and missile attack on Kyiv overnight between May 23 and 24, utilizing an Oreshnik hypersonic intermediate-range ballistic missile, marking an escalation of hostilities. Despite the severity, cryptocurrency markets did not show an immediate significant response. However, the ongoing conflict and the use of stablecoins for circumventing sanctions could lead to increased regulatory actions in the crypto space.
sourceName: Geopolitical Tensions and Their Impact on Cryptocurrency Markets (via Vertex AI Search)
title: Russia Launches Hypersonic Missile Attack on Kyiv

details: Negotiations between the United States and Iran are reportedly in their final stages, with US lawmakers divided on the potential agreement. This geopolitical uncertainty, combined with broader risk-off sentiment, contributed to Bitcoin falling below key resistance levels, extending a subdued weekly performance. Macroeconomic concerns, including expectations of tighter monetary policy from the US Federal Reserve, also weigh on crypto markets. Additionally, Iran has introduced a cryptocurrency-based ship insurance initiative for the Strait of Hormuz, raising concerns about sanctions evasion and security risks.
title: US-Iran Deal Progresses Amid Lawmaker Divisions; Bitcoin Falls

details: A recent report revealed that at least £325 billion of "dirty money" flows through the UK annually, a sum equivalent to over 10% of its GDP. The report calls for a "pause" on government plans to establish London as a global crypto hub, citing concerns that such a move could exacerbate issues related to money laundering and illicit financial activities linked to crypto assets.
title: UK Crypto Hub Plans Questioned Over "Dirty Money" Concerns
